subject.title: [Bug] web_fetch fails in dual-stack networks when DNS returns IPv6 special-use addresses

question: Should OpenClaw relax default SSRF DNS-answer handling so a hostname with mixed allowed and blocked resolved addresses may proceed using only the allowed candidates?
rationale: The code change is bounded, but it changes a security boundary for outbound web_fetch behavior and should reflect maintainer intent rather than an automated policy guess.

options.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
options.body: Allow the request only when at least one resolved address is allowed, remove all blocked addresses before pinning, and keep all-blocked result sets hard-failed.

options.title: Keep any-blocked fail-closed
options.body: Treat any blocked DNS answer as intentional fail-closed SSRF behavior and document affected users toward trusted proxy or fake-IP opt-in configuration where applicable.

options.title: Make mixed polluted DNS explicit opt-in
options.body: Preserve the current default and add or reuse an operator-controlled policy path for environments that intentionally trust polluted DNS handling.

recommendation.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
recommendation.body: Allow the request only when at least one resolved address is allowed, remove all blocked addresses before pinning, and keep all-blocked result sets hard-failed.

likelyOwner.reason: The central SSRF policy assertion and current security-boundary history most directly point to Peter Steinberger for this decision.
